citations.assessment: Names Rav Acha bar Yaakov in the derivation about time-bound commandments. The passage supplies no location or academy.
Identifies the Pappunian authority as Rav Acha bar Yaakov. This is evidence of geographical association.
Names Rav Acha’s enactment at Pappunya on account of thieves.
Acha counts himself within the group of sixty, then states that he alone escaped the reported consequence.
The Gemara describes him borrowing and repaying. Rashi explicitly explains the fixed study time, livelihood by day, and repayment by night.
Rava praises him to Rav Nachman and calls him a great man.
Rava’s sharp response follows Acha bar Yaakov’s explanation of the recurring Temple service.
Reports the knife episode at Rav Acha’s place. The Gemara calls Acha exceptional in its alternative explanation.
Rabbi Levi states the interpretation, which Rav Acha expounds in Pappunya. The narrative says that Satan kissed Rav Acha’s feet.
Acha’s arrow saying occurs while waving his lulav. The passage cautions against provoking Satan. Heilprin proposes two explanations for the difference from Pelimo.
Pelimo says it every day. This explains the contrast Heilprin draws, while his proposed explanations remain attributed.
The preceding expression for Torah scrolls supplies the object for Rav Acha’s calfskin scroll. The bracket preserves the unresolved exact spelling behind מ״ת.
The story tells of the seven-headed being losing one head per bow. Abaye’s academy and hoped-for miracle are in the preceding segment.
The pointed-to entry expressly identifies Acha with the earlier husband in the cited reincarnation account.

The cited exposition includes the heads, Jacob’s seven bows and Shema, and the snake–Acha initials. It names Moses as the one who wished to remove the snake. The English preserves Heilprin’s irregular local wording, with this note identifying the explicit subject in the source.

evidence.witness: Megaleh Amukot, based on Krakow, 1637 edition

citations.assessment: Tosafot reports a tradition that Rav Acha asked the question concerning giving it to an Israelite child.
Tosafot cites Rabbenu Chananel’s identification and Rashi’s lack of a stated locus.
Names Rabbi Elazar of Hagrunya as the person punished. The companions participate in the preceding episode, whose Tachlifa patronym is not uniform across adjacent units. Heilprin uses a plural verb.
Rabbi Ilai transmits in Rabbi Acha bar Yaakov’s name, in our master’s name. Rashi specifies Rav, without independently settling the pupil relation.
Explicit Rav Acha report in Rabbi Zeira’s name.
Chiyya of Hormiz-Ardashir reports what Acha bar Yaakov related in Rav Nachman bar Yaakov’s name.

The parallel dossier cites Sanhedrin. The inspected Bavli names Rav Chama while the inspected Ein Yaakov has Rav Chisda. The digital Bavli does not support the further Rav Acha reading that Heilprin reports.

evidence.witness: En Jacob, translated by SH Glick, 1916
